description:
FILED s521 (Fable, 2026-10-18 19:0x) from the #3494 umbrella CENSUS (docs/ioc-row-census-s521.md, a read-only Opus agent; Fable re-probed the reproducer on main 81afe6b0 vs perl 5.40.3 before filing).  PRE-EXISTING: identical on the 5e6e241d, ed8a4504 and 0b836815 extractions (not s521a's #3433, not #3516).

REPRODUCER (scratchpad rv/newb.pl):
    use Symbol; my $s = 1;
    my $c = bless Symbol::gensym(), 'Foo'; $c = \$s; print ref($c), " ", ($c == \$s ? "same" : "other");
    my $u = Symbol::gensym(); $u = \$s; print ref($u);      my $h = {}; $h = \$s; print ref($h);
perl 5.40.3: `SCALAR same SCALAR SCALAR`.   PCL main: `Foo other REF SCALAR` -- a scalar whose current value is a typeglob (a glob ref: gensym, IO::File, `\*FH`) does not take the new scalar ref: the assignment lands somewhere other than the variable's box (the glob's own SCALAR slot? `$$c = \$s` would do exactly that), so the variable still answers the old glob; hash and scalar referents are fine.

WHERE IT BITES: IO-Compress t/compress/multi.pl's outer `my $cc` holds an IO::File in the filehandle pass; the buffer pass does `$cc = $output` (`\$compressed`); on PCL `$cc` still holds the closed IO::File, Gunzip->new reads it ("Header Error: Minimum header size is 10 bytes"), `isa_ok $gz` fails (row 1226) and the next `$gz->read` dies -- the `*PLAN*` stop at 1227 of 1829 in all four 107multi files: 8 blessed rows + 602 x 4 = 2,408 rows that never run.

FIX SHAPE: cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, the box STORE path (`p-setf` / the scalar assignment arm) when the box's current value is a glob object -- the store must replace the box's value, never write through to the glob's scalar slot (the #423 "glob value = glob ref" box model: read docs/ir-spec.md's glob section and DECIDED ## s421 #423 first); design it WITH #3516 (the same representation, s521d) -- a glob VALUE in a scalar (`$x = *FH`) vs a glob REF in a scalar (`$x = \*FH`) must both take a plain reassignment.  Probe BEFORE / AFTER vs perl: the reproducer; `$x = *STDOUT; $x = 5; print $x`; `$x = \*STDOUT; $x = [1]`; `*$c = \$s` (the GLOB-slot assignment, which must still write the slot); `$$c = \$s` on a gensym (perl: writes the glob's SCALAR slot).  ACCEPTANCE: the reproducer = perl; IO-Compress 107multi-* one-file runs past row 1227 (their `*PLAN*` rows re-attributed or removed by edit; the newly reached rows blessed with causes); a guard row in `Pl/t/bless-referent-01.t` or the glob file, inverse FAILS on main; a cl/ change: the sweep + op/gv.t uni/gv.t one-file companion runs (TIMEOUT files: compare C_ok).


=== DONE (s521e, 2026-10-19, commit 164eac80) ===
CAUSE: box-set set the box's is-ref flag only when the NEW value was a typeglob and never cleared it, and its class-clear rule did not count a typeglob as a reference holder -- so after `$c = \$s` the box kept is-ref t (ref() read REF, `==` the box's own address) and the old class (Foo).  FIX (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp box-set): when the OLD value was a typeglob and the new one is not, is-ref is cleared and the class goes with it.  SECOND SHAPE found while probing: `$$e = \$s` on a gensym wrote $e ITSELF (ref($e) REF); perl's rv2sv of a glob ref is the GV, so it is the GLOB assignment `*$e = X` -- new arm in (setf p-cast-$) routes a box holding a typeglob with is-ref through p-glob-assign-dynamic (perl: `GLOB` and `${*$e}` = 1, NOT the ref -- the brief's expectation "the ref" was wrong; perl is the oracle).
PROBES (scratch/s521e/pr/g1.pl, 13 lines) = perl 5.40.3: the reproducer, `$x=*STDOUT;$x=5`, `$y=\*STDOUT;$y=[1]`, `*$d=\$s`, `$$e=\$s`, `local $L=\$s` over a glob, hash value, array element, @_ alias, glob VALUE then a ref.
BAR: guard Pl/t/bless-referent-01.t t14 (inverse: base-aff112d7 prints `t14:Foo other REF REF REF REF`); IO-Compress 107multi-gzip / -deflate / -rawdeflate / -zip one-file runs 1829 pass / 0 fail each (were 1226/1 + PLAN stop at 1227 of 1829): the 8 #3519 rows LEFT baselines/cpan-board14-fails.tsv by edit; ir-spec row beside "$$globref vs ${*glob}".  Sweep + op/gv.t uni/gv.t companion: see the s521e session-log section.
subject: SILENT WRONG (pre-existing): a scalar that holds a GLOB REF keeps the glob when assigned a SCALAR REF -- `my $c = bless Symbol::gensym(), 'Foo'; $c = \$s; ref $c` is Foo (perl SCALAR), `$c == \$s` false; an unblessed gensym gives REF.  IO-Compress multi.pl reuses an outer `$cc` that held an IO::File, so Gunzip reads the dead handle: 107multi-* stop at 1227 of 1829 = 8 rows + 2,408 never run.  The #423 glob box model; design with #3516
